name: Crack a fetch on turn 1-2 for a non-basic land that unlocks a hand card
intent: On turn 1 or 2, once open-land-unlocks, open-shock-unlocks and open-fetch-unlocks have all had first refusal, play a fetch from hand and crack it for a library land that unlocks some other hand card even though that land is not a basic - any of this deck's four basic-type fetches reaching Steam Vents (Island Mountain: its Mountain subtype alone is enough, so every fetch that can search for a Mountain reaches it, not only the ones that can also search for an Island) to unlock Preordain. Thundering Falls is never a target here - it has no such 'you may pay life' clause and always enters tapped (its own printed text carries no condition at all), so it can never flip a hand card's own `unlocks` fact to true regardless of what a fetch's search could find. Item 4 (2026-09-14 review batch): open-fetch-unlocks' own true key narrowed from unlocks_by_search to unlocks_by_basic_search, closing the boros-aggro known limit (a fetch that can only reach a shock should never be treated as a free unlock), but that leaves prowess with no play at all for a hand whose only blue route is a fetch reaching a non-basic Steam Vents - this deck's blue is genuinely scarce (only Steam Vents and Thundering Falls carry the Island subtype at all, and Thundering Falls never unlocks), unlike devoted-combo where every fetch can also reach a basic Forest. This lane closes that gap, priced correctly: it pays the fetch's own 1 life to crack plus the found land's own optional 2, strictly worse than either open-land-unlocks (free) or open-shock-unlocks (one payment only) - so it stands down whenever either of those, or open-fetch-unlocks itself (which would find a free basic instead), already would. The choose_cards pick shares open-fetch-unlocks' own missing-subtype-first prefer order (item 5) since the same reasoning applies once more than one non-basic land is reachable. Only turns 1-2, land drop available, mine, precombat main, empty stack.
